Steps
1. In the editor, select the left widget and open Styles; then select the right widget. Both swatches look white.
2. Open Preview and click the moon icon (dark mode).
3. In the editor, try to return the left widget to the default.
Expected
The panel shows the difference between "no colour set (follows light/dark)" and "white", and offers a way back to the default.
Actual
Both swatches look white (#ffffffff and #ffffff) but they are different: the left has white saved, the right has nothing saved and shows the default. In dark mode the right turns grey and the left stays white. There is no Reset in the colour row; the only way back is fx on, clear the text, fx off.
Test data
Left: Background color #ffffffff saved (what the colour picker saves for white)
Right: nothing saved (the default)

text.value: 6. "Default" and "white" look the same in the Styles panel

The body tag style was also dropped before this change (the box was white), so this is a gap against the agreed rule rather than a regression.
Steps
1. Open Preview on this page.
2. Compare the two widgets.
Expected
Both widgets are dark green. Rule from the thread (Devang): "if the background color attribute is there in the Raw Html, it should overwrite whatever is set in the styles."
Actual
Left (background on the body tag) is pink with black text. Right (same colours on a wrapper div) is dark green. The rule holds for a wrapper div or a style tag, not for the body tag.
Test data
Both widgets: Background color #FDE2E4
Left Raw HTML: <body style="background:#0B3D2E;color:#ffffff"><p style="margin:8px">Hello from the body tag.</p></body>
Right Raw HTML (control): <div style="background:#0B3D2E;color:#ffffff;height:100%;padding:8px;box-sizing:border-box">Hello from a full-height wrapper div.</div>

Steps
1. Open Preview on this page and look for anything broken: an error message instead of a widget, a blank page, or errors in the browser console.
2. In the editor, select a few of these widgets and open Styles: the panel must open normally.
3. Compare each box with the controls: fx red (red) and fx false (white default).
Expected
Nothing breaks. Values that are not a colour fall back to the white default.
Actual
See the result printed under each widget. Values that are not a colour make the box see-through (the blue container shows) instead of falling back to white.
Test data
Every widget sits on a Container with background #DCEBFF and has Raw HTML <p style="margin:8px">Plain paragraph, no colours of its own.</p>
Group A: the value is an fx expression returning each JavaScript type. Group B: plain text values.
Not on this page: fx BigInt(5), which stops the whole page from rendering in any property (a general binding problem older than this change).
